- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows sharp decline, model often overreacts; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects; apply a 1–2% downward bias to prevent lagged reversal.
- If sentiment change is volatile (±0.67+), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates true price when sentiment is rising; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment >0.75 over last 5 days.
- If news volume is constant (3.0) and sentiment is flat (±0.33), model tends to drift; apply 0.5–1.0% correction toward historical mean.
